patch.value: Automatic semantic session attribution: infer bounded topic and role from claimed work and harness context without per-call identity flags

The shipped session-context contract can carry topic and role, but it depends on a caller declaring them once. Live history on 2026-08-03 contains 43,765 events with zero topic observations and zero role observations, including fresh Codex mutations whose four provenance dimensions are all null. Add an SDK-first inference layer that derives a stable, privacy-bounded topic from the claimed or focused pm lineage and derives a controlled role from the operation sequence and harness context. Precedence is explicit session declaration, trusted harness-native metadata, claimed or focused work, then explicit unavailable. The mutation record must preserve value, source, confidence, rule version, and the item or session evidence used, without retaining prompt text. Inference updates incrementally when focus or claims change and propagates through CLI, SDK, MCP, child processes, and packages.

A fresh CLI, SDK, MCP, child-process, and package-host mutation made after claiming or focusing an item records a non-null topic derived from the canonical item lineage without any PM_AUTHOR, author, topic, or role flag; Role values come from a versioned controlled vocabulary such as implementer, reviewer, investigator, release operator, planner, or orchestrator and are inferred from claim state plus mutation sequence rather than copied from a boolean environment flag; Each inferred observation records source, confidence, inference-rule version, and stable evidence references; raw prompt text, arbitrary session contents, paths, and secrets are never retained; Explicit session declarations and trusted harness-native values take precedence over inference, conflicts are reported, and an explicit unavailable reason is recorded when evidence is insufficient; Inference is incremental and bounded by the active lineage or session delta, not a scan of the full corpus, with million-item and thousand-agent latency and memory budgets; CLI, SDK, MCP, extension, and child-process mutations share one SDK implementation and produce equivalent provenance; A corpus-facing coverage gate measures topic and role by harness and source, proves a negative control can fail, and ratchets non-null coverage without rewriting legacy history; Session topic and role improve adaptive-context and episode-trajectory relevance in a graded evaluation without increasing the declared observation token ceiling
Make topic and role useful, automatic, explainable, and queryable on every mutation without PM_AUTHOR or repeated agent input
Fleet history can be grouped by what agents were doing and in which capacity without relying on free-text author names

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Corpus census of the provenance block, taken 2026-08-09 evening over every history stream in the tracker. This is the coverage measurement this item's gate criterion calls for, taken once by hand so the criterion has a baseline to ratchet from.

Population: 46,439 history entries, of which 6,893 carry a provenance block at all, which is 14.8 percent. Within those 6,893, the dimensions populate at four different rates and none of them is close to complete. Model is set on 284 entries, 4.1 percent, always from a probe source. Version is set on the same 284. Effort is set on 986, 14.3 percent, always from the environment. Role is set on 407, 5.9 percent. Topic is set on 425, 6.2 percent.

The finding this item exists for is in the topic distribution, and it is sharper than the null it was filed against. Topic is no longer null — it is populated, and every one of the 425 populated values came from the argv source, and all 39 distinct values are item identifiers. The field named for the session's subject is being filled with the object of the individual invocation. This is worse than null for the purpose the criterion states, because a null topic is visibly absent and an argv-derived one is invisibly wrong: any consumer grouping work by topic gets one group per item touched rather than one group per session, and the grouping looks successful. A coverage gate that measures non-null topic rates would score this as progress.

The related role finding is legacy and must not be re-filed. Role carries the literal value 1, from the environment, on 264 entries, and the separate value implementer, from argv, on 143. The 264 boolean-valued rows run from 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-08 and stop there; pm-eq9dlw closed on 2026-08-09 with a resolution that added bounded corpus-wide value-domain scanning reporting these as legacy. No boolean-valued role has been minted since that fix, so the closure is sound and the rows are immutable history, not an escape.

Two consequences for this item's acceptance criteria, neither of which changes their wording. The criterion requiring a versioned controlled vocabulary inferred from claim state rather than copied from an environment flag is confirmed as still unmet on the topic dimension as well as the role dimension, and for the same underlying reason: a dimension is being filled from whatever nearby value is syntactically available rather than from evidence about the session. And the corpus-facing coverage gate the criterion requires should measure per-dimension non-null rate broken down by source, not just by harness, because a gate blind to source would have reported topic coverage rising from zero to 6.2 percent and called it progress on exactly the day the wrong value started being written.

Method note for whoever implements the gate: the block is per-entry and optional, so the denominator question is live here in the same shape horizon AI describes. Coverage over entries carrying a block is 6.2 percent for topic; coverage over all entries is 0.9 percent. The gate must declare which denominator it speaks for.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Provenance baseline measured 2026-08-10 from a live mutation, so this item's remaining scope is now precise rather than inherited.
Read directly off the newest history entry of a freshly created item, with no PM_AUTHOR set and no --author passed anywhere in the session:
author            harness:claude-code
author_source     detected
agent_harness     claude-code
agent_model       claude-opus-5      source probe
agent_instance    b006a2086429d635675530d7
agent_provenance  effort  xhigh        source environment
role    implementer  source argv
topic   pm-ob9z4y    source argv
version 2.1.226      source probe
So harness, model, thinking effort and harness version are all resolved automatically and correctly, and the role dimension no longer records the boolean child-session flag that pm-eq9dlw was filed for — it reads implementer. Every field carries its own source, which is the property that makes the remaining gap legible instead of guessable.
What is left is exactly the semantic half this item names, and the source labels prove it. role and topic both read source argv. topic resolves to the id of the item the command happened to mutate, and role to a value inferred from the command shape. Both are mechanical proxies: they are correct as provenance and wrong as attribution. A session that touches forty items records forty different topics, none of which is the session's subject, and a session that reviews rather than implements still records implementer because the verb it used was an update.
The consequence for the record is that topic and role cannot be aggregated. Grouping history by topic yields one bucket per item, so the question this dimension exists to answer — what was this session about, and in what capacity was the agent acting — is unanswerable even though the field is populated. A null would at least be honest; an argv echo reads as adopted while behaving as absent, which is the same failure shape pm-pcys9n recorded for the release field.
Two constraints for the inference this item will add. It must not overwrite a probe-sourced or environment-sourced value, since those are ground truth and the semantic layer is not. And it must record its own source distinctly, so an inferred topic is never mistaken for a declared one; source inferred alongside the existing probe, environment and argv vocabulary.
